edition.name: Migne PL 3 (1844), Epistola Firmiliani ad Cyprianum, via Corpus Corporum / Latin Wikisource
edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: Vide qua imperitia reprehendere audeas eos qui contra mendacium pro veritate nituntur. Quis enim justius indignari contra alterum debuit? utrumne qui hostes Dei asserit, an vero qui adversus eum qui hostes Dei asserit pro Ecclesiae veritate consentit? Nisi quod imperitos etiam animosos atque iracundos esse manifestum est, dum per inopiam consilii et sermonis ad iracundiam facile vertuntur, ut de nullo alio magis quam de te dicat Scriptura divina: Homo animosus parat lites, et vir iracundus exaggerat peccata. Lites enim et dissensiones quantas parasti per Ecclesias totius mundi? Peccatum vero quam magnum tibi exaggerasti, quando te a tot gregibus scidisti! Excidisti enim te ipsum. Noli te fallere; siquidem ille est vere schismaticus qui se a communione ecclesiasticae unitatis apostatam fecerit: dum enim putas omnes a te abstineri posse, solum te ab omnibus abstinuisti. Nec te informare ad regulam veritatis et pacis vel Apostoli praecepta potuerunt monentis et dicentis: Obsecro ergo vos ego vinctus in Domino, digne ambulare vocatione qua vocati estis, cum omni humilitate sensus et lenitate, cum patientia sustinentes invicem in dilectione, satis agentes servare unitatem spiritus in conjunctione pacis; unum corpus, et unus spiritus, sicut vocati estis in una spe vocationis vestrae. Unus Dominus, una fides, unum baptisma, unus Deus et pater omnium, qui super omnes, et per omnia, et in omnibus nobis.
pass_a_gloss: See with what lack of skill you dare to rebuke those who strive for truth against falsehood. For who ought to be more justly indignant against another? Whether he who claims that they are enemies of God, or truly he who consents to the truth of the Church against him who claims that they are enemies of God? Except that it is clear that the unskilled are also reckless and irascible, while through lack of counsel and speech they easily turn to irascibility, so that divine Scripture says about no one more than about you: A reckless man prepares lawsuits, and an irascible man exaggerates sins. For how many lawsuits and dissensions have you prepared throughout the Churches of the whole world? How great a sin have you exaggerated for yourself, when you cut yourself off from so many flocks? For you have cut yourself off. Do not deceive yourself; for he is truly a schismatic who has become an apostate from the communion of ecclesiastical unity; for while you think that all can be kept away from you, you have kept yourself away from all. Nor could the Apostle's precepts, warning and saying, inform you according to the rule of truth and peace: I therefore beseech you, bound in the Lord, to walk worthily of the calling with which you have been called, with all humility of mind and gentleness, with patience bearing with one another in love, being eager to preserve the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace; one body, and one Spirit, as you have been called in one hope of your calling. One Lord, one faith, one baptism, one God and Father of all, who is above all, and through all, and in all of us.

pass_b_english: Look at the lack of skill with which you dare to rebuke those who strive for truth against falsehood. For who ought more justly to be indignant against another: the one who claims they are enemies of God, or the one who agrees with the truth of the Church against the one who claims they are enemies of God? Except that it is clear that the unskilled are also reckless and irascible, since through lack of counsel and speech they easily turn to anger, so that divine Scripture says about no one more than about you: A reckless man prepares lawsuits, and an irascible man exaggerates sins (Proverbs 18:6; 29:22). For how many lawsuits and dissensions have you prepared throughout the churches of the whole world? How great a sin have you exaggerated for yourself, when you cut yourself off from so many flocks? For you have cut yourself off. Do not deceive yourself; for he is truly a schismatic who has become an apostate from the communion of ecclesiastical unity; for while you think that all can be kept away from you, you have kept yourself away from all. Nor could the apostle's precepts, warning and saying, inform you according to the rule of truth and peace: I therefore beseech you, bound in the Lord, to walk worthily of the calling with which you have been called, with all humility of mind and gentleness, with patience bearing with one another in love, eager to preserve the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace; one body, and one Spirit, just as you were called in one hope of your calling. One Lord, one faith, one baptism, one God and Father of all, who is above all, and through all, and in all of us (Ephesians 4:1-6).
